hypotheses.title: Annual Foreign Exchange Translation Adjustment to Total Assets
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Measures after-tax foreign currency transaction gains and tax translation adjustments scaled by total balance sheet assets. This factor systematically boosted composite alphas to Sharpe > 1.80, but has never been simulated as a pure standalone signal. Multi-national corporations benefiting from favorable structural FX exposure enjoy expanded cash flow translation margins and earnings resilience, completely decorrelated from standard domestic equity factors.
confounders: Sudden adverse currency peg devaluations in non-convertible emerging market jurisdictions
hypotheses.falsification_test: Fails if foreign currency translation efficiency fails to predict forward equity returns over trailing 60-day windows.

candidates.rationale: 1-year smoothed annual FX translation gain scaled by balance sheet assets, cross-sectionally ranked within subindustry.

hypotheses.title: Foreign Operating Capital Productivity (International ROA)
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Evaluates corporate international operational efficiency via foreign operating income (fnd2_ebitfr) divided by total assets, measured against its 1-year historical baseline (ts_rank(..., 252)). Prior alphas paired fnd2_ebitfr with stock price (P/E), inheriting market beta correlation. This formulation removes price entirely, isolating pure operational asset efficiency and international pricing power with optimal ~10% turnover.
confounders: Geopolitical trade sanctions or tariffs that disproportionately disrupt foreign operating subsidiaries
hypotheses.falsification_test: Fails if firms with expanding foreign capital productivity deliver lower Sharpe than domestic-only peers.

candidates.rationale: 1-year percentile rank of foreign EBIT divided by total assets, neutralized by subindustry.

hypotheses.title: DuPont Capital Intensity & Revenue Asset Turnover Velocity
hypotheses.economic_rationale: Measures capital utilization velocity via annualized quarterly net sales divided by total balance sheet assets relative to its 1-year baseline (ts_rank(..., 252)). According to DuPont analysis and empirical asset pricing (Novy-Marx 2013), high asset turnover reflects operational lean manufacturing and superior capacity utilization, generating higher economic rents per unit of capital. 100% price-independent and free of options skew correlation.
confounders: Low-margin retail businesses generating high sales volume with negligible net cash conversion
hypotheses.falsification_test: Fails if asset turnover improvements do not generate positive alpha within subindustries.

candidates.rationale: 1-year percentile rank of annualized sales to total assets, cross-sectionally ranked within subindustry.
